shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling/needs/work/storage come free from vanilla. Levels and per-level size are bought from a 146,000-cell budget; colder with altitude, richer ore and more cave with depth. Coast, river and lake tiles supported; Dubs Mint Minimap and Map Preview both patched. Rendering, interaction and generation all verified in play.
body:
# As above, So below II — V2

> V1 is **DELETED**. ~61 files / ~16,400 LOC.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

> **Visuality pass (runs #167-171) COMPLETE — all seven reported items closed and verified in play.**
> Shadows on every upper level · water visible from above · rivers generate · water no longer runs north-south · snow-line seeding removed · Map Preview patched · Dubs Mint Minimap patched. Coastal tiles were fixed along the way as an eighth item.

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount × Slot)`; bands along **+z** from the deepest basement; permanently-fogged gutter between bands; `Slot = ceil((bandHeight+2)/64)×64` — **64-alignment is load-bearing**. Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 254, each just under a 64 boundary.

### The one insight
`Region.Neighbors` is **topological, not spatial**. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms/temperature/vacuum; `Reachability.CanReach` works **unpatched**. **But reachability ≠ a path** — 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

### Hard 1.6 constraints
Path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell ⇒ **total stacked cells is the runtime metric** · no `PathFinder.FindPath` · `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE — the recurring shape of every generation bug
The surface band is a horizontal SLICE of a tall map, so **anything vanilla anchors to the map's extent lands in the wrong band**. Three instances, each with a different fix shape:
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Anchor** — a point picked as a fraction of `Size.z` | river / lake centre (§6b) | remap the point |
| **Field** — a gradient centred on the map centre | coastline (§6e) | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| **Noise space** — a slice ≠ a short map | Map Preview (§6d) | generate at full height, then crop |
**Classify a new generation bug into one of these three before theorising.** Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all use `FalloffAtAngle`).

# 2. LEVEL PLAN — cell budget = **146,000**
`4 × 190 = 145,920` sets the figure; `2 × 254 = 130,048`, `7 × 126 = 112,896`; `5 × 190` and `7 × 190` refused (3-up-and-3-down at 190 auto-drops to 126 — the intended trade).
`ABMapSizeLimit` owns it: `UpperLevels`/`LowerLevels` (0-3), `BandCount`, `SurfaceBand = lower`, `Fits`, `MaxSize`, `MaxLevelsFor`, `StackedCells`. `ABV2.BandCount`/`SurfaceBand` are properties (were consts — the only thing pinning the mod to 3 levels).

### ⚠ THE CHOOSER UI — own the widget, don't patch the data
**`Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play.** Vanilla's group headers only render for 200/250/300, so their presence in a screenshot proved our array was never used. The postfix also re-snapped `GameInitData.mapSize` **every frame**, undoing every click.
**Now:** our own radio buttons write `mapSize` directly; vanilla sizes locked; strip shows cells-used-vs-budget. Window grown via an `InitialSize` postfix — **vanilla lays its columns from the top and never consults the height, so added space is ours.**

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix → tick sweep → `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` **BFSes the band graph**; hops must strictly decrease or pawns ping-pong.
**Caveat:** an intermediate level must be walkable between arrival and the next staircase. **STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING — three wrong layers before the right one
`GetOptions` clickPos (wrong layer) → per-pawn `BestOrderedGotoDestNear` (fought vanilla's formation) → **correct:** `RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 don't") is the proof: only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Fix = normalise `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band. **Verified.**

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE — `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated `drop`. **NINE systems share it**, including both shadow layers and `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen`.
**SEVEN appearances of the single-`- Slot` bug.** #6/#7 were the shadow layers — from +1 the step lands on the opaque surface and works; from +2/+3 it lands in OPEN AIR, which holds no edifices. **VERIFIED FIXED (#168): shadows correct on every upper level.**
**Sun-shadow subtlety:** its mask is *neighbour*-based (a mountain-edge caster sits under an opaque cap and can never resolve a descent of its own), so mask and descent are answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, taking the **smallest** drop among the nine cells.
**Still single-band:** the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire).

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION — verified in play
**⚠ FOUR REJECTED ATTEMPTS:** force-linked wall masks · high-queue cover · wall-sprite suppression · theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Despeckle (**wall dissolves only at 7+ open neighbours** — at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge) · one central fog hole · five-terrain plateau palette · cliff faces · alpine pass (shallow-only tarns, per-cell 6-cell edge rule, rim scree, exposure-thinned flora).
**Cross-band decoration:** `EmitMassSilhouetteAt`/`EmitMeadowFadeAt` emit into ANY layer at a z offset.
**Ore glyph bug:** ore defs have no `naturalTerrain` ⇒ a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole **atlas sheet** per cell.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER — `ABWaterV2.cs`. **1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect**
`SectionLayer_Watergen` renders `waterDepthMaterial` into the **WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's** texture; the visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that (`_WaterOutputTex`) **at its own screen position**. Printing the water material where the depth pass never wrote yields **nothing at all**.
- **Water vanished from upper levels — VERIFIED FIXED (#171).** Half a two-pass effect was missing. `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` mirrors vanilla's `internal` Watergen (`waterDepthMaterial` + water-to-water edge fans for shorelines), descends via `TryResolveVisibleBelow`, **overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`**. Proven by the bisect toggle: water below vanishes with the pass off and returns with it on.
- **Rivers "did not generate" — VERIFIED FIXED (#167).** `GetRiverCenter` picks `Rand.Range(0.3f,0.7f) × map.Size.z`. Remapped into the surface band preserving the *roll*. Patched on `GetRiverCenter`, **not** `Init` (Init consumes it immediately); the delta/confluence/headwater/island variants inherit it. **`GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first** — `River.Init` prefers an existing `lakeCenter`. Proof: `band 0 baseRiver=3079`, all others `0`.
- **Water ran north-south even in lakes — RESOLVED, most likely as a side effect of the river fix.** The ghost-river theory (a river generated into a sky band, carved away, but its flow field still computed and sampled by surviving water) is the surviving explanation; no longer reproduces. Not independently proven — if it ever returns, the tarn discriminator is the tool.
- **⚠ REJECTED — DO NOT RETRY: republishing `_MapSize` as one band.** Fitted every symptom including its uniformity; **DISPROVED IN ONE LAUNCH** — banding the global is what MAKES water run north-south. Airtight because `surfaceBand=0` made the fold the identity, so flow data was bit-identical and `_MapSize.y` was the only variable. The folded REPEAT-wrapped flow texture went with it.

# 6c. DUBS MINT MINIMAP — active level only. **VERIFIED (#169)**
Reflection-only, **no foreign type in any signature** (HarmonyBoot's class processor resolves parameter types when walking a patch class — the old Rimefeller ghost-warning bug). Detection by **type presence**, not packageId.
**ONE RECT, NOT SEVEN PATCHES.** Their six draw passes all take the same `radarRect` and are LINEAR in position. Solving for the rect that lands the active band in the window gives `height = view.height*Size.z/H`, `y = view.height*(H + bandMin - Size.z)/H`. Their unmodified passes then place every marker correctly. **Culling is free** — other bands map outside the existing `GUI.BeginClip`.
**Their texture blit cannot be reused:** `DrawTextureFitted(rect, tex, 1f, 1f)` binds to `(Rect, Texture, float scale, float alpha)` and fits **preserving the TEXTURE's aspect** — a 190×768 stack letterboxes into a sliver and silently stops agreeing with the marker rect. Drawn with `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`.
`UpdateMapTex` prefixed to refresh **only the active band**; `procCell` bound as a real delegate (per-cell hot). We never reinitialise their texture (`Resize`→`Reinitialize` renamed across Unity versions). `CameraDriver.CurrentRealPosition` is **private** (Dubs publicises Assembly-CSharp); `Find.Camera.transform.position` is the same value. Clip/group pops in a `finally`.

# 6d. MAP PREVIEW — surface band only. `MapPreviewCompat.cs`. **VERIFIED (#171)**
Map Preview never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap` — it builds a bare Map and runs a short genstep list on a worker thread, so our banding prefix never fires. Harmless if the surface band were an ordinary square map, but it is a SLICE, and every genstep samples **position-based noise**: rows 384-510 of a 190×768 map bear no relation to rows 0-189 of a 190×190 one. **A different map, not a slightly wrong one.**
**Fix = generate at full stacked height, show only the band's rows.** Same size, seed and noise coordinates ⇒ correct by construction.
**Most of it is NOT Harmony.** Their `ModCompat_BetterMapSizes` is the precedent: `MapSizeUtility.MaxMapSize`/`MapSizeOverride` are public static fields. `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise (default 500; a stack reaches 896) — the widget's texture and pixel buffer are built from it and `QueuePreviewRequest` **throws** when MapSize > TextureSize. Only z rises; x still clamps quest-site previews. Must be set before the window first opens (the widget is a field initialiser that snapshots it).
Three patches for what has no hook: postfix `DetermineMapSize` (the CLAMPED entry point, so our value survives) gated to player-colony parents — a quest `Site` must keep its `PreferredMapSize`; postfix `MapPreviewResult.get_TexCoords` to crop — **TexCoords already exists to draw a sub-rect of an oversized buffer, and v maps straight to cell z because pixels are `Pixels[z*TextureSize.x + x]` and `SetPixels` treats index 0 as bottom-left**; postfix `OnWorldTileSelected` to restate window width (they size it `scale = PreviewWindowSize / max(x,z)`, so a stacked size yields a tall sliver). Plus a tooltip-cell fix.
**`TryPendingSurfaceRect` falls back to a SIZE-INFERRED layout** so every generation-time patch behaves identically during a preview. Safe because we chose that size and `Slot ≥ bandHeight + 2`, so `bandCount * Slot` always exceeds the width once more than one band exists.
**Known cost:** previews generate 4-7× the cells on their worker thread.

# 6e. ⚠ COASTLINES — coastal tiles are multi-level. **VERIFIED (#171)**
Symptom (#170): a coastal colony generated with its **entire surface band underwater** — the start-spot search reported `36100 water` out of exactly 36100 cells. **100%, not "mostly", and that precision was the diagnosis**: a lake cannot do it (radius is 0.6× the map WIDTH, so band corners always stay dry), only a map-spanning coastline can. Safety nets held (clearing carved, 4 pawns rescued) but the colony was an ocean.
**THE FALLOFF IS NOT SCALED WRONG, IT IS CENTRED WRONG.** In `MapNoiseUtility.FalloffAtAngle` the gradient's size comes only from `map.Size.x` (`DistFromAxis_Directional(x/2)`, translate by `x*(0.5-offsetPct)`). `map.Size.z` appears in exactly ONE place: the final `Translate(-x/2, 0, -z/2)` parking the field on the map centre. So the coast gradient is **already one band wide** and merely sits at the middle of the whole STACK; a surface band hundreds of cells from a ~190-wide gradient is fully saturated.
**Fix is a coordinate rewrite, not a rebuild:** `z' = (z % Slot) + (map.Size.z - bandHeight) / 2`. The modulo puts every band on the same rows (ocean in the same place on every level — what a stacked coastal colony wants); the offset re-centres the band on the field's centre, giving exactly the window an ordinary bandHeight-tall map would see.
**NO SCALING, deliberately.** Stretching band-local z to span the full height is the obvious "fit" and would skew every non-axis-aligned coastline (the rotation happens INSIDE the module) and make the displacement noise anisotropic, smearing beach detail.
**ONE PATCH COVERS THE FAMILY:** Bay, Cove, Fjord, Peninsula, Archipelago, CoastalIsland, CoastalAtoll, Iceberg, Lakeshore all derive from `TileMutatorWorker_Coast` and **none override `GetNoiseValue`** — the single point where the field is read, by both the elevation and terrain passes. Map comes from `MapGenerator.mapBeingGenerated`, which also makes it work inside a Map Preview.
V1 got this free by giving each level its own Map; V2 has to earn it.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Sky temp `-4°C × level` (compounds) · basement flat -6 · ore `×(1+0.45×(depth-1))`, cave openness `×(1+0.35×(depth-1))`, both AFTER the settings clamp · mountains taper upward for free.
**Snow line:** generation-time seeding **REMOVED** (a pre-frozen top level read as a different biome instead of higher ground). Nothing lost: vanilla melts/accumulates per-CELL temperature and the per-level offset already makes high levels cold — earned, not painted on at t=0.

# 8. CAMERA
`freeCameraPan` REMOVED. `ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by **level**; **`maxZoom` left DERIVED** (an absolute would mis-scale a 190 band). `Dialog_ABCameraCalibration` opens with the clamp UNLOCKED — **a calibration tool must suspend the limit it calibrates.** Clamp bails while `Scribe` is active or state isn't `Playing`.

# 9. ⚠ GENERATION COST — the top open item
| Config | Tile | Cells | Carve | Things destroyed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 × 190 | — | 109,440 | 5.0 s | 14,971 |
| 7 × 126 | — | 112,896 | 30.4 s | 62,686 |
| 4 × 190 (#167) | **river** | 145,920 | 18.7 s | 56,318 |
| 4 × 190 (#168) | sparse | 145,920 | 2.5 s | 15,787 |
| 4 × 190 (#169) | sparse+road | 145,920 | 2.1 s | 13,913 |
| 4 × 190 (#171) | **coast** | 145,920 | 15.2 s | 50,585 |
**`Sky clear` is ~97% of the carve**; **`0 rocks spawned`** — everything destroyed is content generated into doomed bands and immediately deleted.
**⚠ THE REAL DRIVER IS BIOME CONTENT, NOT CELL COUNT.** At *identical* 4×190, carve ranges 2.1-18.7 s — a **9× spread** driven entirely by what the tile generates. **Any carve timing MUST record the tile or it is meaningless.** Rich tiles (river, coast) are the worst case; sparse ones are nearly free.
Band 1's sky clear is consistently ~3× bands 2-3. **THE FIX — extend the doomed-band genstep skip** (precedent: `Patch_WildPlantSpawner_ABSkipDoomedBands`, 16.9 s → 4.2 s). Targets: `RocksFromGrid`, `Terrain`, `RockChunks`, `Plants`, `ScatterRuinsSimple`, `CaveHives`.
**HARD CONSTRAINT: per-cell gensteps scope safely; `map.Area`-count scatterers do NOT.** **Do not blanket-skip the water/coast mutators** — §6b/§6e depend on them running correctly anchored, and §6d shares those patches.

# 10. RUNTIME PERF — 59.6 fps @96 pawns, mod ≈2% frame. All rendering is bake-time section-mesh geometry.

# 11. VERTICAL LINKS — elevator SHIPPED, **untested**. Full-mesh 2×2; O(n²) in band count.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
band info · **below layer report** · below pawn report · **water report** (per-band water/withDepthMat/baseRiver census + riverGraph + `_MapSize`) · transit health · stuck probe · transit logging · lighting/shader/biome reports · bisect toggles (incl. **below water depth**, which is what proved §6b) · ABGenProfile · camera calibration.
**The start-spot failure log is a first-class diagnostic** — its cell census ("0 unstandable, 0 edifice, 36100 water") identified the coastline bug in one line.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **Doomed-band genstep scoping pass** (§9) — now the clear top item; band 1 first, and record the tile.
2. **Audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators** — Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley carry §6e's mis-centring but do not share its sampling hook.
3. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router (needs a stair tower), elevator, reload fix, lake-anchor patch (no lake tile rolled yet).
4. Realtime-things pass still single-band (motes/fire >1 level down).
5. Selection bracket **drifts upward as you zoom out** — that path mixes world and screen space; our offset is in world units.
6. **Option E — waterfalls**: now genuinely de-risked, since below-view water is proven (§6b).
7. COMBAT never verified · Option C (stepped mesa) parked · vertical conduit · compat audit incl. Better Mountains co-load · transplant (still the clean long-term answer to slicing) · **store page still says three levels**.

# 14. LESSONS (telegraphic)
**Run the diagnostic before the third theory** · **build the A/B discriminator INTO any change whose mechanism you cannot read** — the `_MapSize` theory fitted every symptom and was still WRONG; the toggle cost one launch instead of a release · **a beautiful fit is not evidence** · **an EXACT number is a diagnosis** — "36100 of 36100 water" ruled out lakes by arithmetic alone · **the ABSENCE of a known error line is a valid pass signal** · **poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts** — single-occurrence `[RimWorld]` warnings are filtered, and one was ours · **when N call sites share ONE linear mapping, re-aim the shared parameter instead of patching N sites** (Dubs: one rect replaced seven patches; the existing clip did the culling) · **find the ONE virtual everything funnels through** — nine coastal mutators, zero overrides of `GetNoiseValue` · **read the foreign mod's OWN compat classes first** (`ModCompat_BetterMapSizes` turned half of Map Preview into two field assignments) · **check which OVERLOAD a foreign call binds to** · **a foreign mod's publicised Assembly-CSharp lets THEM touch private members you cannot** · **never put a foreign type in a patch-class signature** · **re-centre, don't rescale** — scaling a rotated noise field skews the angle and makes displacement anisotropic · **read what a helper actually depends on before assuming it needs a rebuild** — `FalloffAtAngle` uses `Size.z` once, for centring · **anything anchored to the map's extent lands in the wrong band; classify it as anchor / field / noise-space** · **position-based noise means a SLICE of a tall map ≠ a short map** · **an odd/even or count-dependent symptom is arithmetic** · **a UNIFORM symptom is a scale/constant, a PATCHY one is data** · **when a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes** — 1.6 water is two · measure, don't extrapolate · **two runs of the same config are only comparable if the TILE matches** (9× spread) · **a single-step assumption survives until the data has two steps — grep every `- Slot`; SEVEN times now** · **patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it, when the storer consumes it immediately** · **own the widget instead of patching the data it reads** · never hide sprites that carry gameplay information · ore defs have no naturalTerrain · a `Graphic_Linked` base material is the whole ATLAS SHEET · **"can't happen" fallbacks are what the player photographs** · enforce spatial rules PER CELL · **balance GUI clip/group pops in a `finally`** · statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak — CWT, or store the id only as a change DETECTOR · **Unity textures are not GC'd with their owner** · **any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`** · never cache comps while Scribe active · FinalizeInit = worker thread · `SectionLayer` subclasses are **auto-discovered** by `Section`'s ctor.

## TESTING RULE
`isolated=true`. Companions: drop them when a bug might not be ours (#167-171 all ran clean with none). **Compat tests need the target mod as a companion** — Dubs (`dubwise.dubsmintminimap`) and Map Preview (`m00nl1ght.MapPreview`) are both INACTIVE in the user's real list. Multi-level tests need `quicktest=false`; **Map Preview doubly so** (the preview only exists on the world map). **Water tests need a river or lake tile; coastline tests a coastal one** — and note the tile in any perf comparison. **A `surfaceBand=0` config cannot exercise band-folded addressing** — use lower levels for that.
